Hon'Ble Shri Justice Vivek Rusia
 &
 Hon'Ble Smt. Justice Anuradha Shukla
 On The 11th Of November, 2024
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 19396 of 2022
 State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Versus
 Asir Ali And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Beerendra Kumar Upadhyay - Advocate for applicant.
 Order
Per: Justice Anuradha Shukla

The present application has been filed by the State under Section 378(III) of the Code of Criminal Procedure against the judgment dated 03.12.2021 passed by First Additional Judge to the Court of Ist Additional Sessions Judge, Panna (M.P.) in Sessions Trial No.49/2015 and Sessions Trial No.02/2018 decided commonly.

entities.text: Court of Ist Additional Sessions Judge, Panna (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Under this judgment, the respondents were acquitted of the charges of Section 420, 467 (467/34), 400 and 471 (471/34) of IPC.
Additionally, respondent Nos.1 to 4 were acquitted of the charge of Section 468 (468/34) while respondent No.5-Lal Bahadur @ Betu was acquitted of the charge of Section 474 of IPC.

2. The facts of the case may be summed up as a confidential information was received by Rajnath Mishra posted as Van Parichetra NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:55544 2 MCRC-19396-2022 Adhikari in Van Parichetra, Singhpur, District Satna, that wood from Babool Tree was being transported under a fake transit permit; accordingly, truck No.UP78CN6716 was stopped at the check-post and search was made; it was transporting tree wood but the transit permit under which this transportation was being made was apparently fake, as it did not bear the signature of Van Parishetra Adhikari, Shri Rajnath Mishra; there were three persons travelling in that truck; Shri Rajnath Mishra got the FIR registered against all the three occupants i.e. Asir Ali,
Mohammad Naim and Tajuddin Ahmad and Crime No.55/2015 was registered in Police Station Devnagar, Panna.

The matter was investigated and it was revealed that forged transit permit was given by respondent No.4-Kamta Prasad Sonkar and respondent No.5-Lal Bahadur @ Betu to the State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Asir Ali on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12521717/
1 rest of the respondents who were found travelling in the truck.

entities.text: State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Asir Ali
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, charge-sheets were filed against the respondents and the trial was held.
All the respondents were acquitted by the trial Court holding that the prosecution failed to prove any of the charges against the respondents.

3. This petition for grant of leave to appeal has been argued on the ground that the prosecution story was duly proved by the evidence but the learned trial Court failed to appreciate the evidence in correct perspective and illegally acquitted the respondents.
It was also ignored that no evidence was produced in defence still the trial Court gave a finding of acquittal.

The decision of Apex Court in Phula Singh Vs. State of H.P. AIR 2014 SC 1256 was evidently ignored which requires that an explanation is supposed to be given by the accused in his examination under Section 313 of Cr.P.C.
regarding any incriminating evidence produced against him and if he remains NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:55544 3 MCRC-19396-2022 silent then inference has to be drawn against him.

entities.text: Phula Singh Vs. State of H.P. AIR 2014 SC 1256
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the basis of these submissions, a request has been made to grant permission under the petition to appeal against the impugned judgment.
4. Learned counsel for the State has been heard at length and the record of trial Court is perused.

5. It is a case where the allegation of cheating, forgery and using forged documents has been made against the respondents, therefore, the most crucial document would have been the transit permit which was allegedly forged document.
Exhibit-P/3 is the photocopy of transit permit which has been certified to be the true copy by the Investigating Officer, Hari Singh Thakur (PW-8).
His entire testimony fails to give details about the existence and whereabouts of the original transit permit.

The statements of complainant Shri Rajnath Mishra (PW-1) are also lacking in details whether the original transit permit was recovered from any of the respondents and if yes then to whom that original document was handed over.
No case of forgery can be made out unless the alleged forged document is produced in evidence in original.
6. For establishing a case of forgery, it was required to be proved by the prosecution that the original transit permit did not have the signature of issuing authority.

Shri Rajnath Mishra (PW-1) has claimed that he was exercising the authority to issue transit permit and according to him,
questioned transit permit was not having his signature.

His specimen signature were obtained during investigation and were sent to the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:55544 4 MCRC-19396-2022 handwriting expert for examination of signature appearing in the questioned document.
The handwriting expert report was produced in evidence as Exhibit-P/42 but it was never proved through the testimony of expert.
Further, this report failed to give any definite opinion regarding authorship of read enclosed questioned signature stamped and marked as Q1.
This inconclusive report completely demolishes the prosecution case regarding forgery of signature of authorized person on the questioned document.

It is strange that after examining and comparing the signatures of Rajnath Mishra on two documents the expert was not able to give any definite opinion while Shri Rajnath Mishra was denying his signature on questioned document by merely seeing it with bear eyes and that too without giving any details on this denial.

7. Statements of Krishna Kumar Vishwakarma (PW-2) and Gyan Chandra Pandey (PW-3) who were the members of the search party, could at the most prove the checking of questioned transit permit State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Asir Ali on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12521717/
2 but their testimony is not relevant to establish that the questioned transit permit was a forged document.

entities.text: State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Asir Ali
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Anwar Ahmed Siddiqui (PW-4) has though claimed that questioned transit permit was not issued by his office but this statements was given when the original book under which the transit permits were being issued was not before him.

Jagdish Kumar Sonkar (PW-5), Mohan Singh (PW-6)
and Awadhesh Sharma (PW-7) are the witnesses to the proceedings undertaken during investigation, having no bearing on the question of forgery of transit permit.

8. Considering all these facts in their entirety, we find no reason to NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-JBP:55544 5 MCRC-19396-2022 upset the finding of the court below regarding acquittal of respondents.
Hence, leave to prefer appeal against the impugned judgment of acquittal is hereby denied.
9. The petition is, accordingly, dismissed and disposed of.
10. Let record of the trial Court along with copy of this order be sent back to the concerned court for information.
(VIVEK RUSIA)

(ANURADHA  JUDGE JUD  NP State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Asir Ali on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12521717/
